If you've been missing the ability to double-click the Digital Crown to bring up the Apple Watch app switcher from before watchOS 27, it looks like that feature is set to return in watchOS 27.2 beta 2. Here are the details.

Apple is bringing back the watchOS app switcher

Apple pushed watchOS 27.2 beta 2 to developers this morning, less than a week after the previous beta 1 release.

This beta version contains a detail that should please long-time Apple Watch users, including my colleague Zac Hall. Earlier this month, he wrote about how watchOS 27 removed the ability to quickly switch to recently used apps by double-clicking the Digital Crown.

He noted in his article that users no longer had any way to quickly jump to recently used apps, and he hoped Apple would restore the gesture before watchOS 27's official release or in a future update.

Although Apple has not restored the Digital Crown shortcut for the app switcher in watchOS 27.2 beta 2, it has indeed reintroduced the app switcher with a new gesture.

According to a discovery on the Apple Den Discord server, shared by user Bones on X, watchOS 27.2 beta 2 lets users bring up the app switcher by long-pressing the bottom of the screen while inside an app.

As Bones pointed out in a tweet, the app switcher largely works the same as before: after long-pressing the bottom of the screen to launch the switcher, users can rotate the Digital Crown to browse recently used apps, or swipe left on an app and tap the "X" button to remove it from the switcher.

As with any beta, there's no guarantee this exact method will make it to the final release (expected next month), but the addition in watchOS 27.2 beta 2 shows Apple is listening to user feedback and finding ways to bring back the app switcher.

Have you been missing the app switcher in watchOS 27? Let us know in the comments.
